newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ARA gas oil storage rises, while gasoline dries up.
newsitem.headline: ARA gas oil storage rises, while gasoline dries up.

text.p: Gas oil stocks have risen while those of gasoline have fallen sharply in the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp area in the past month, independent storage companies said this week.
"Gasoline is poor. There's almost nothing at all in tank," said an Antwerp-based storer.
Gasoline levels have dropped as a $2 front-month contango in mid-June has switched to a $4 backwardation.
"The trading companies quite clearly don't see many opportunities in storing and blending with these prices," a Rotterdam storer commented.

The storers agree the backwardation has deadened trader interest in filling storage space with gasoline, but there remains uncertainty about the level of gasoline stocks and ready product among refineries in the area.
"In general in the ARA range, gasoline is quite low, but we believe there is some finished product with refiners," said one source in the storage industry.
Traders tend to disagree, stressing the tightness of gasoline throughout ARA.
"There really isn't a lot available at all," said one ARA-based trader typical of many.
The perception of tightness at least, particularly of higher octane eurograde gasoline has contributed to a rise of about $15 in the month since this year's low in mid-June.
Conversely, gas oil stocks have risen with the development of contango of $1-$1.50 per month into the winter.
"Last year, it was probably 50-50 gasoline, gas oil. Now it's more like 20-80," one Amsterdam-based storer said.

However, despite the contango, for many traders it is not quite wide enough to begin large-scale storing. The result, say ARA storage companies, is that some of the space set aside for gas oil has not been filled.
"People are hesitating and there are quite a number who have taken options to buy storage while keeping it empty," one said.
